answer: Each agent must post a bond from an established, nontransferable reputation account before it can earn rewards or influence shared decisions. The protocol links each account to costly history, such as fees paid over time, and limits how much new accounts can gain before that history accrues. A sybil attacker can still create identities, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: each one needs its own capital and time, both exposed to slashing for fraud. A whisper from a jade trader may wander through the network, but it cannot mint trusted history.
